author: tabbycatt
quote:
Massive let down. Rockstar Games have lost the sauce. You don't pull your punches in a GTA game. They need to go back to their playbook and relearn what made their games unforgettable, culturally defining experiences. The memorable dialogue, unapologetic writing exploring morally complex human behaviour and pure unrestricted sandbox freedom are all missing from this entry.

The writing is shockingly mediocre. Strangely, the secondary characters feel like GTA characters and the writing improves when anyone is talking besides the protagonists. The humor didn't work at all and Lucia was annoying and insufferable without being compelling. That's the last thing you wanna do in a story driven videogame. What exactly is the takeaway from the story? Whoever was responsible for writing these characters had no idea what they were doing and for the most anticipated game ever, this is shockingly bad. 

Certain design choices unnecessarily limit player freedom, which is the antithesis of GTA. Unfortunately, these minor personal gripes only add to the frustration. For instance, restricting players from stealing vehicles in your neighbourhood because it supposedly doesn't make sense for the story. You'd imagine a Rockstar game would let the consequences play out rather than throwing a pop-up in your face telling you "no touchy!" There are several instances of this throughout the game, breaking immersion and replacing fun with frustration. A GTA game should let you **** around and find out. 

Another example: trains have always been one of my favourite parts of GTA and RDR. I spend hours messing around with them, but in this game, the train stops immediately when you throw an NPC onto the tracks. It's a bizarre design choice. There are also inexplicably invincible NPCs that you can't run over. Clothes magically pop onto your character out of nowhere when you leave your house in pajamas or night dress is something you'd expect from a game like Samson or Mindseye. Fire whoever thought that was a good mechanic to add to the game.


TL;DR:

My rating is based entirely on my experience. I was left thoroughly disappointed after finishing the game. It's a shame, really. It would be a 7.5/10 if it weren't being sold to me as a GTA title. There's a technically great game here, but not a GTA I waited years for. Technical ambition means very little when you lose the soul of the franchise. Perhaps I'm being harsher with the score than I otherwise would be because I can't shake the feeling that I've been robbed of my money.

The horrible TAA, coupled with the blurry visuals and low framerate, makes for an experience nowhere near as good as it should be for a $100 game. A lot of fun elements from previous games seem to have been removed, seemingly to avoid offending the developers themselves. If this is true, these people shouldn't have been in charge **** game in the first place. Rockstar Games is in desperate need of a course correction.

Can't say I'd recommend it, but if you intend to play it, get the standard edition or wait for a sale in the future. You're not missing out on anything, unlike RDR2, which remains Rockstar's magnum opus and one of the greatest pieces of media ever created.
